newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. Liberia mission renewed to help with elections.
newsitem.headline: U.N. Liberia mission renewed to help with elections.

text.p: The Security Council unanimously approved on Thursday a three-month renewal of a 92-member U.N. observer mission in civil war-torn Liberia, enabling it to help with elections scheduled for May 30.

The elections are the highlight of a peace accord signed in Abuja, Nigeria, last August, ending a civil war that erpted in December 1989. More than 150,000 people were killed in the fighting, which devastated the country's mining and rubber economy.
The U.N. Observer Mission in Liberia (UNOMIL) works with a 10,000-strong peacekeeping force called ECOMOG, fielded by the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS).
The elections are being organised on the basis of a framework agreed between Liberia's council of state and ECOWAS.
The Security Council, in its resolution to renew the mission until June 30, welcomed recommendations in a recent report by Secretary-General Kofi Annan for UNOMIL to assist with the election process.
This will include helping produce and broadcast a daily radio programme to ensure voters receive neutral, factual information.

In view of the May 30 election date, the council said it was concerned at the delay in installing a new independent elections commission and a reconstituted supreme court, which is to adjudicate any disputes.
The commission will comprise seven Liberian citizens -- three to be appointed by the former warring factions and four from civil society.
The parliament will comprise a 64-member House of Assembly and a 26-member Senate. Voting will be on the basis of proportional representation.

The council urged the international community to provide financial, logistical and other assistance for the election process and additional support for ECOMOG to enable it to sustain a secure environment.
All Liberian parties were urged to cooperate in the peace process, including respect for human rights and facilitating humanitarian activities and the disarmament of ex-fighters.

According to Annan's report, 20,332 out of an estimated 33,000 fighters were disarmed under UNOMIL supervision during an official disarmament period between Nov. 22, 1996, and Feb. 9, 1997. A total of 21,315 fighters, including 4,306 childen under the age of 18 and 250 female fighters, were demobilized by the U.N. humanitarian assistance coordination office.

The Security Council also stressed the importance of helping with the prompt repatriation of refugees willing to return to Liberia in time to register and vote. An estimated 768,000 Liberians, out of a population of about three million, have sought asylum in neighbouring countries.
The council resolution reminded all states of their obligation to comply strictly with an embargo on the delivery of weapons and military equipment to Liberia.
Annan was asked to keep the council regularly informed of the situation and to submit a new report by June 20.
